module.tech_cves.checks: Looks up known vulnerabilities (CVE) in OSV.dev for the detected frameworks and software with their version: Django, Laravel, Symfony, Drupal, Joomla, Next.js, Angular…
module.tech_cves.fix:
For each piece of software in the finding, move to the version given by "Fixed from" or to a newer one. Read the release notes for breaking changes and test on a copy of the site first.
Check the version actually installed before concluding: the version announced by the site may be hidden, frozen by a cache, or patched by the distribution without changing number. Useful commands: `composer show`, `pip show`, `npm ls`.
If a major upgrade is not possible without development work, install the latest patch release of the branch that is still maintained, or apply the workaround from the vendor's advisory, and restrict access to the affected feature.
Use your package manager's tool to list then fix vulnerable dependencies: `npm audit`, `composer audit`, `pip-audit`, `bundle audit`, then update the lock file.
Servers (nginx, Apache, IIS, PHP) are not covered by OSV.dev: check their version against the vendor's or your distribution's security advisories, and apply system updates.
Enable automatic alerts (Dependabot, Renovate, a subscription to the vendor's advisories) and schedule regular updates, for example monthly.
Run the scan again: if the announced version stays old, clear the CDN cache and check that the right server was updated.
module.tech_cves.fix_snippet:
# npm
npm audit
npm install package-name@latest

# Composer
composer audit
composer update vendor/package-name

# pip
pip install pip-audit
pip-audit
pip install --upgrade package-name
module.tech_cves.title: Technology vulnerabilities
module.tech_cves.why: A vulnerable framework or CMS version is one of the most exploited entry points. Servers (nginx, Apache, PHP) are not covered by OSV.dev.
